summary: Notes the background pass writes now name people the way Nora does. It used to read each member under their own self-set profile name, so a note could call someone by a name no live turn uses.
details: The pass that notices arrangements worth writing down read the room's messages without the roster, so every message it saw was signed with the sender's self-set platform profile name. Every live turn reads the roster name instead (DEC-80), so a note and the turn that later reads it named the same person two different ways.
The pass now resolves each sender through the roster before it reads the batch, exactly as a live turn does. A sender the roster does not know keeps their profile name, as before.
The room-culture pass reads the same messages and is unchanged.
limitations: Notes already written keep whatever names they were written with; nothing rewrites them.
Names inside the messages themselves (what the group calls each other) are unchanged; only who SENT each message is resolved.
